past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: Which of the following statements is TRUE about the image formed by a convex mirror?
options: C. It is smaller than the object.
D. It is always formed at the principal focus.
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished (smaller than the object) image behind the mirror for any real position of the object.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: Two capacitors of capacitance 6 µF and 3 µF are connected in a series across a cell of 18 V. The equivalent (effective) capacitance will be
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: For two capacitors connected in series, the equivalent capacitance $C_{eq}$ is given by $\frac{1}{C_{eq}} = \frac{1}{C_1} + \frac{1}{C_2} = \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{1 + 2}{6} = \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$. Thus, $C_{eq} = 2\text{ \mu F}$.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: All of the following are the precautions which should be taken during installation of any electrical equipment EXCEPT
options: A. turn off any attached peripherals.
B. wear shoes with non-conductive rubber soles.
C. attach the electrical equipment to the AC power.
D. disconnect any telecommunication lines from the system.
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Attaching the equipment to active AC power during installation is a hazard and can lead to electric shock. Precautions involve keeping power disconnected until installation is complete, turning off peripherals, wearing non-conductive shoes, and disconnecting telecommunication lines.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text:
The electric force of repulsion between two electrons at a distance of 1 m is
(Note: The value of the constant of proportionality is $9 \times 10^9\text{ Nm}^2/\text{C}^2$ and the charge on electron is $1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$.)
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Using Coulomb's law: $F = \frac{k \cdot q_1 \cdot q_2}{r^2} = \frac{9 \times 10^9 \times (1.6 \times 10^{-19}) \times (1.6 \times 10^{-19})}{(1)^2} = \frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 2.56 \times 10^{-38}}{1} = 23.04 \times 10^{-29} = 2.304 \times 10^{-28}\text{ N}$.

crqs.question: Explain how a gold-leaf electroscope is used to detect the presence and nature (sign) of an unknown electric charge.
crqs.answer: Bringing a charged body near the brass disc causes the gold leaves to diverge. If the electroscope is first charged with a known sign, an increase in divergence indicates the same sign of charge, whereas a decrease indicates the opposite sign or an uncharged conductor.

erqs.question: i. Why can large electrostatic charges be dangerous? Give TWO examples from daily life. ii. Why do long vehicles carrying inflammable materials touch the ground with metallic chains?
erqs.answer: i. Electrostatic discharge creates sparks that can ignite fuel vapours (e.g., aircraft refuelling sparks) or cause lightning strikes. ii. Metallic chains conduct accumulated static charge safely to the Earth (earthing), preventing sparks near inflammable vapour.
erqs.source: AKU-EB SSC-II Model Paper II Q.7(a)

numericals.problem: Calculate the electrostatic force of repulsion between two electrons separated by a distance of 1.0 m in air (k = 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C², q_e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C).
Two capacitors of capacitance 6 µF and 3 µF are connected in a series across a cell of 18 V. The equivalent (effective) capacitance will be
numericals.solution: For two capacitors connected in series, the equivalent capacitance $C_{eq}$ is given by $\frac{1}{C_{eq}} = \frac{1}{C_1} + \frac{1}{C_2} = \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{1 + 2}{6} = \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$. Thus, $C_{eq} = 2\text{ \mu F}$.

numericals.problem:
The equivalent capacitance of the given combination of the capacitors will be
(Note: $C_1 = 5\text{ \mu F}$, $C_2 = 5\text{ \mu F}$, $C_3 = 5\text{ \mu F}$ connected in parallel based on standard textbook diagram layouts)
numericals.solution: Looking at standard parallel combinations for identical capacitors in AKU-EB problems where three equal capacitors are in parallel: $C_{eq} = C_1 + C_2 + C_3 = 5 + 5 + 5 = 15\text{ \mu F}$.

numericals.problem: If two capacitors $C_1 = 6\ \mu\text{F}$ and $C_2 = 12\ \mu\text{F}$ are connected in series, then the equivalent capacitance will be
numericals.solution:
For two capacitors connected in series:
$\frac{1}{C_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{1}{C_1} + \frac{1}{C_2} = \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{2 + 1}{12} = \frac{3}{12} = \frac{1}{4}\ \mu\text{F}^{-1} \implies C_{\text{eq}} = 4\ \mu\text{F}$.
